'''Emmanuel Emovon''', [[Order of the Niger|CON]] (February 24, 1929 – February 20, 2020) was a [[Nigerian]] professor of [[chemistry]] and former [[Vice-chancellor|vice chancellor]] of the [[University of Jos]].<ref>{{Cite news|url=http://sunnewsonline.com/new/professor-emmanuel-emovon-con/ |location=Lagos, Nigeria|title=Professor Emmanuel Emovon, CON |accessdate=June 7, 2015 |url-status=dead |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20150708031527/http://sunnewsonline.com/new/professor-emmanuel-emovon-con/ |archivedate=July 8, 2015 |newspaper=[[The Sun (Nigeria)|The Sun]]}}</ref> 
In 1983, he was elected as president of the [[Nigerian Academy of Science]] and succeeded Professor [[Umaru Shehu]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nas.org.ng/fellowship/members-of-council/ |title=Members of Council |work=Nigerian Academy of Science |accessdate=June 7, 2015 |url-status=dead |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20150707061854/http://www.nas.org.ng/fellowship/members-of-council/ |archivedate=July 7, 2015 }}</ref>

==Early life and education==
Professor Emovon was born in February 1929 in [[Benin City]], [[Edo State]], Southern [[Nigeria]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://allafrica.com/stories/200212060049.html|title=Nigeria: Emovon, Emerges Nepa Customers' Chairman|work=allAfrica.com|accessdate=June 7, 2015}}</ref> He died on February 20, 2020.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.pmnewsnigeria.com/2020/02/20/breaking-nigerias-ex-minister-emovon-is-dead/|location=Lagos, Nigeria|title=Nigeria's Ex-Minister Emovon Is Dead|accessdate=March 3, 2020|newspaper=[[P.M. News]]}}</ref>

He attended Edo College Benin City, where he obtained the West African School Certificate in 1949. He proceeded to the University College, Ibadan now [[University of Ibadan]] for an intermediate Bachelor of Science degree course but obtained a bachelor's degree in [[chemistry]] from the [[University of London]] and doctorate degree from the same university.<ref>{{Cite news|url=http://thenationonlineng.net/new/coming-era-of-penny-pinching/|location=Lagos, Nigeria|title=Coming era of Penny pinching|accessdate=June 7, 2015|newspaper=[[The Nation (Nigeria)|The Nation]]}}</ref>
He was the first Nigerian to obtain the Ph.D. degree of the University of London in physical chemistry in 1959.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Mindex Publishing|url=https://www.mindexpublishing.com/this-is-my-life-by-e-u-emovon/|website=www.mindexpublishing.com|access-date=2020-05-30|archive-date=2021-05-18|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210518095450/https://www.mindexpublishing.com/this-is-my-life-by-e-u-emovon/|url-status=dead}}</ref> He later returned to Nigeria to join the Department of Chemistry, University of Ibadan, as an academic staff (Lecturer II).
He became a professor of chemistry in 1971 and was appointed vice chancellor of Jos in 1978.<ref>{{Cite news|url=http://www.vanguardngr.com/2013/08/asuu-and-nigerian-universities-have-gone-to-seeds/|location=Lagos, Nigeria|title=ASUU and Nigerian universities have gone to seeds |accessdate=June 7, 2015|newspaper=[[Vanguard (Nigeria)|Vanguard]]}}</ref>
In recognition of his outstanding contributions to academics in Nigeria, he was conferred with a National award of [[Order of the Niger|Commander of the Order of Niger]] by [[Olusegun Obasanjo]], the former [[President of Nigeria]].
.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nigeriaheadlines.com/news/professor-emmanuel-emovon-con|title=Professor Emmanuel Emovon, CON|work=Nigerian Headlines|accessdate=June 7, 2015|archive-date=July 9, 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150709170815/http://www.nigeriaheadlines.com/news/professor-emmanuel-emovon-con|url-status=dead}}</ref>

== Awards and recognitions ==

* Professor Emovon was a holder of the traditional Chieftaincy title: The Obayangbona of Benin Kingdom 
* A recipient of the National Honour Award of Commander of the Order of the Niger (CON), 
* Fellow of the Nigerian Academy of Science (FAS) and 
* Justice of the Peace (JP) amongst others

== Family ==
Professor Emovon was happily married to Princess Adesuwa of the Benin Royal Family Oba Akenzua and they are blessed with three daughters and three sons.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Emovon, ex- minister of science and tech. passes on -|url=https://www.thenewsnigeria.com.ng/2020/02/20/emovon-ex-minister-of-science-and-tech-passes-on/|date=2020-02-20|website=The NEWS|access-date=2020-05-30}}</ref>
